tip: Keep commit messages imperative: 'Fix navigation bug' rather than 'Fixed navigation bug'.
Use 'git commit --amend --no-edit' to quickly fold staged changes into your previous commit.
Use 'git restore --staged <file>' to unstage files without discarding your local edits.
Use 'git diff --stat' for a quick visual overview of changed lines and files.
Use 'git stash -u' to stash untracked files along with tracked modified files.
Use branch protection rules on main to require pull request reviews before merging.
Boy Scout Rule: Always leave the code cleaner than you found it.
Functions should do one thing, do it well, and do it only.
Prefer descriptive variable names over cryptic abbreviations. 'userAccount' beats 'ua'.
Avoid magic numbers. Replace literal numbers with meaningful named constants.
Return early to reduce nested if/else indentation (Guard Clause pattern).
Don't comment on 'what' the code does; comment on 'why' it was done that way.
Use dict.get('key', default) instead of direct indexing to avoid KeyError exceptions.
Use enumerate() instead of range(len(items)) when you need both index and element.
Leverage context managers (with open(...) as f:) to guarantee resource cleanup.
Use collections.defaultdict to avoid checking if keys exist before appending values.
Use list and dict comprehensions for concise, readable data transformations.
Use type hints (typing / def func(x: int) -> str) to catch bugs early in IDEs.
Use optional chaining (user?.profile?.avatar) to prevent undefined crashes.
Use nullish coalescing (val ?? 'default') instead of || to allow empty strings or 0.
Prefer 'const' by default, 'let' only when reassignment is needed, never 'var'.
Use Promise.allSettled() when running multiple promises where you care about all results.
Use structuredClone() for deep copying objects without JSON serialization hacks.
Avoid 'any' in TypeScript; use 'unknown' when the type is truly dynamic.
Always pass key props to mapped list items based on stable IDs, not array indices.
Keep component state as close as possible to where it is used to avoid unnecessary rerenders.
Use React Server Components for heavy server-only dependencies and data fetching.
Use next/image for automatic image optimization, WebP conversion, and lazy loading.
Clean up useEffect listeners, timers, or abort controllers in the return cleanup function.
Order Dockerfile commands from least to most frequently changed to maximize layer cache.
Use multi-stage Docker builds to keep production container images tiny and secure.
Never run container applications as root; specify 'USER node' or 'USER nonroot'.
Always pin base image versions (e.g. node:20-alpine instead of node:latest).
Use .dockerignore to exclude node_modules, git histories, and local secrets from images.
Premature optimization is the root of all evil. Profile actual bottlenecks before optimizing.
Enable HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 and Brotli/Gzip compression on your production servers.
Debounce rapid user inputs (search bars, resize handlers) to reduce CPU cycles.
Implement pagination or infinite scroll instead of loading thousands of records at once.
Leverage Redis or in-memory caches for expensive database queries with high read ratios.
Never commit secrets, tokens, or .env files to source control. Always .gitignore them.
Always sanitize and validate user input on both client and server sides.
Store passwords using Argon2id or bcrypt with high work factors, never plain SHA/MD5.
Set Content-Security-Policy (CSP) headers to prevent Cross-Site Scripting (XSS).
Avoid 'SELECT *' in production queries; request only the columns you actually use.
Add indexes on columns frequently used in WHERE, JOIN, and ORDER BY clauses.
Use database transactions (BEGIN/COMMIT) for multi-step data mutations to ensure consistency.
Use connection pools instead of opening a brand new database connection on every request.
Use Ctrl + R in your terminal to search backwards through command history quickly.
Use 'htop' or 'btop' instead of plain 'top' for visual system resource monitoring.
Use 'set -e' (or set -euo pipefail) in bash scripts to fail immediately on errors.
Design APIs to be idempotent: retrying a failed network request should be safe.
Aim for high cohesion and loose coupling between system microservices and modules.
